kids: Watch the City Hall holiday tree light up
See Santa visit before the holiday season begins
site: Dunedin City Hall, Louden Avenue side
about: The City of Dunedin describes its tree lighting ceremony as a beloved way to kick off the holiday season, with the whole community gathering for the lighting of the city's holiday tree.
The ceremony takes place in front of City Hall on the Louden Avenue side, and the city lists the entertainment as the International Chorale along with a special visit from Santa.

The city's holiday guide names the tree lighting as the first stop in its list of 2026 holiday events, ahead of Breakfast with Santa and the Holiday Boat Parade on December 5 and the downtown parade on December 12.
Dunedin Parks and Recreation presents the event, and families can call 727-812-4530 with questions. Admission is free.
The holiday guide also notes that Operation Twinkle lights up the downtown with festive spirit through the season.
Dunedin sits on the Gulf side of Pinellas County, and its downtown is known for a walkable Main Street, so many families make an evening of it with a short stroll after the lights come on.
The city organizes this tree lighting as part of a run of December gatherings, which makes the first Thursday of the month a natural start for families planning several outings.
The holiday guide places the tree lighting at 5 PM, ending at 6:30 PM, which leaves families the rest of the Thursday evening for dinner downtown.
faq: When is the Dunedin tree lighting in 2026?
Thursday, December 3, 2026, at 5 PM at Dunedin City Hall.
Does it cost anything to attend?
No. The City of Dunedin lists the tree lighting as free to attend.
Where do we stand to watch?
Gather in front of City Hall on the Louden Avenue side at 737 Louden Avenue.
Who performs at the ceremony?
The International Chorale provides the musical entertainment, and Santa makes a special visit.
Who do we call with questions?
Dunedin Parks and Recreation answers questions at 727-812-4530.
What other holiday events follow in Dunedin?
Breakfast with Santa and the Holiday Boat Parade are on December 5, and the Holiday Parade and Old Fashioned Christmas is on December 12.
How long does the ceremony last?
The City of Dunedin lists the tree lighting from 5 PM to 6:30 PM.

kids: Watch lit boats cruise the Intracoastal
site: Dunedin Marina and Edgewater Park, 51 Main Street
about: The Holiday Boat Parade is presented by Dunedin Parks and Recreation, the Dunedin Boat Club and Loggerhead Marker 1 Marina, and the city calls it a return of a Dunedin favorite.
Boats register in advance through the Dunedin Boat Club by December 1. Registration is free, and the city caps the parade at 40 boats, so registration may close early.
The route runs from the waterway outside Loggerhead Marker 1 Marina south along the Intracoastal to Union Street, then north to finish at the Dunedin Marina at about 7 PM.

The city lists accessible parking near the entrance, a dedicated ADA viewing area on the marina's North Peninsula, accessible routes, accessible portable restrooms by the playground on the south side of the park and extra lighting towers after dark.
Event questions go to Dunedin Parks and Recreation at 727-738-2920, and parade questions go through the Dunedin Boat Club website.
Edgewater Park sits along the water at the foot of Main Street, so the parade works as a waterfront evening for families who want lights, music and a boat show in one trip.
Because the parade shares the weekend with Breakfast with Santa, some families treat December 5 as a full Dunedin holiday day.
faq: When is the Dunedin Holiday Boat Parade?
Saturday, December 5, 2026, from 6 to 9 PM, with the boats starting at 6 PM.
Is the boat parade free to watch?
Yes. The City of Dunedin lists the cost as free.
Where is the best place to watch?

Bleachers are set up in the Dunedin Marina parking lot, and the city suggests lawn chairs. Weaver Park, Bayshore Boulevard and Edgewater Drive are other viewing spots, though boats are farther away there.
What else happens in Edgewater Park?
Holiday music, a tree lighting ceremony, s'mores and concessions by Old Bay Cafe, leading up to Santa's arrival.
Can our boat join?
Yes. Registration is free through the Dunedin Boat Club by December 1, with a limit of 40 boats.
Is there accessible viewing?
Yes. The city lists an ADA viewing area on the marina's North Peninsula, accessible parking and accessible restrooms.

kids: Share a wish list with Santa over pancakes
about: Dunedin Parks and Recreation describes the morning as a chance to bring a wish list and join Santa for a pancake breakfast, crafts and entertainment at the Dunedin Community Center.

The city sells tickets through its online registration system, and the holiday guide lists early bird pricing of $10 per person on or before December 2, then $15 per person on December 3 if space allows.
The breakfast falls on the same Saturday as the Holiday Boat Parade, so families can pair the morning with the evening parade at the marina.
The city thanks sponsors EKP, Pisces and Lane's Lemonade on the event page, and it invites teens, adults, groups and nonprofits to volunteer at its holiday events.
Questions go to the Dunedin Community Center at 727-812-4530.
The city offers the lower early bird ticket price through December 2 and raises it by five dollars on December 3, when tickets remain only if space allows.
The community center is a short drive from downtown, so families can attend breakfast in the morning and return downtown later for the boat parade.
Registration runs through the city's online recreation system, where families pick the Breakfast with Santa listing and pay per person for each guest attending.
faq: When is Breakfast with Santa in Dunedin?
Saturday, December 5, 2026, at 9 AM at the Dunedin Community Center.
How much are tickets?
$10 per person for the early bird rate on or before December 2, and $15 per person on December 3 if space allows.
Where do I buy tickets?
Through the City of Dunedin's online registration system, linked from the event page.
What is included?
A pancake breakfast, crafts and entertainment with Santa.
Where is the Dunedin Community Center?
At 1920 Pinehurst Road in Dunedin, Florida 34698.
Who can I call for more information?
Call the Dunedin Community Center at 727-812-4530.
Can we buy tickets at the door?
The city's holiday guide lists tickets through December 3 and only if space allows, so families should buy through the online system ahead of time.

kids: See floats, bands and Santa roll through downtown
Ride in a Clydesdale horse drawn carriage
Slide down the snow slide and roast s'mores
site: Downtown Dunedin, Main Street and Douglas Avenue
about: The City of Dunedin calls the Holiday Parade and Old Fashioned Christmas its most anticipated holiday celebration, running from 3:30 to 9 PM on Saturday, December 12, 2026.
The parade travels along Douglas Avenue from Beltrees Street north to Skinner Boulevard, and Santa Claus arrives in downtown with the final floats.
Immediately after the parade, downtown Dunedin turns old fashioned, with activities and entertainment spread along Main Street and Broadway, plus live music in Pioneer Park and snow flurries.
The city lists Achieva Credit Union as presenting sponsor, Joe's Family Plumbing for the parade, Pisces for carriage rides and Emergent Kids Preschool for the main stage.
The event page links a road closure map and a Jolley Trolley route map, and the free shuttle serves two park and ride lots.
Dunedin Parks and Recreation presents the event and takes questions at 727-812-4530.
Parents with younger children often arrive early for a curb spot along Douglas Avenue, since the parade draws one of the largest crowds of the Dunedin holiday season.
The trolley service lets families skip downtown parking, which is useful on a night when Main Street and several side streets are closed to traffic.
faq: When is the Dunedin Holiday Parade in 2026?
Saturday, December 12, 2026, with the parade starting at 3:30 PM and festivities running until 9 PM.
Is it free?
Yes. The city lists it as free to attend, with donations accepted at the activity areas.
Where does the parade travel?
Along Douglas Avenue from Beltrees Street north to Skinner Boulevard.
What can kids do after the parade?
Ride in a Clydesdale horse drawn carriage, play on a snow slide, do crafts and games, get face painting, roast s'mores and see snow flurries.
Where can kids meet Santa?
At the Dunedin History Museum after the parade.
Where do we park?
Use the free Jolley Trolley from 2:30 to 9:30 PM, parking at the Mease Hospital overflow lot at 722 Virginia Street or at Curtis Fundamental at 531 Beltrees Street.
